# Overview

`imaging-manifest-fork/` contains the FHIR IG source for the **EU Manifest-based Access to DICOM Objects (MADO)** implementation guide (`hl7.fhir.eu.imaging-manifest`, FHIR R4).

It is a **plain fork copy** of the upstream HL7 EU Imaging Manifest repository. There is no git subtree or submodule; upstream sync is done manually.

A similar AI-implementer repo for the HL7 EU Imaging Report IG is [bvdh/hl7eu-imaging-ai-implementer](https://github.com/bvdh/hl7eu-imaging-ai-implementer).

---

# Directory Layout

```
imaging-manifest-fork/
├── sushi-config.yaml          ← IG identity, dependencies, page list
├── ig.ini                     ← IG Publisher entry point
├── input/
│   ├── fsh/                   ← FSH source (profiles, extensions, valuesets, examples)
│   ├── pagecontent/           ← Narrative markdown pages
│   ├── mapping/               ← Mapping tables
│   ├── images/                ← Static images
│   ├── images-source/         ← Editable image sources (PlantUML etc.)
│   ├── includes/              ← Jekyll include fragments
│   └── ignoreWarnings.txt     ← Suppressed publisher warnings
├── fsh-generated/             ← SUSHI output (do not edit manually)
├── output/                    ← Publisher HTML output (do not edit manually)
├── input-cache/               ← Downloaded packages and publisher cache
├── ig-template/               ← IG template overrides
├── _build.sh / _build.bat     ← Primary build entrypoint
├── _genonce.sh / .bat         ← One-shot publisher run
├── _gencontinuous.sh / .bat   ← Watch-mode publisher run
└── _updatePublisher.sh / .bat ← Download/update publisher.jar
```

---

# Building the IG

All build commands must be run from **inside** `imaging-manifest-fork/`.

```sh
cd imaging-manifest-fork

./_build.sh build        # standard build
./_build.sh update       # update publisher.jar, then build
./_build.sh notx         # offline build (no terminology server)
./_build.sh nosushi      # skip SUSHI, re-run publisher only
./_gencontinuous.sh      # watch mode for iterative authoring
```

Use the `build-ig` skill for the full build lifecycle, QA validation, and failure triage.

# Key Configuration

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `sushi-config.yaml` | IG id, canonical, FHIR version, dependencies, pages list |
| `ig.ini` | IG Publisher entry point; references `sushi-config.yaml` |
| `input/ignoreWarnings.txt` | Suppress known non-actionable publisher warnings |

**Current IG identity**
- Package id: `hl7.fhir.eu.imaging-manifest`
- Canonical: `http://hl7.eu/fhir/imaging-manifest`
- FHIR version: R4 (4.0.1)
- Version: `0.2.1-build`

**Key dependencies**
- `ihe.rad.mado: dev`
- `hl7.fhir.eu.base: 2.0.0`
- `hl7.fhir.eu.extensions: 1.3.0`

# Authoring Conventions

- FSH source lives in `input/fsh/`. Do not edit `fsh-generated/` — it is overwritten by SUSHI on every build.
- Narrative pages live in `input/pagecontent/` as `.md` files. Every page referenced in `sushi-config.yaml` under `pages:` must have a corresponding `.md` file.
- Image source files (PlantUML, draw.io) go in `input/images-source/`; rendered images go in `input/images/`.
- `output/` is fully regenerated by each publisher run; never commit hand-edits to it.

**Slice Naming Convention**

All slice names must use **kebab-case** (lowercase with hyphens) consistent with the IHE-MADO parent project. Examples:
- ✓ `identifier[study-instance-uid]`, `identifier[accession-number]`, `identifier[placer]`
- ✓ `endpoint[wado]`, `endpoint[webviewer]`, `basedOn[order]`
- ✓ `extension[ko-document-title]`, `extension[anatomical-region]`, `extension[retrieve-location-uid]`
- ✗ ~~`koDocumentTitle`, `accessionNumber`, `retrieveLocationUid`~~ (camelCase — avoid)

When referencing parent profile slices in FSH rules or examples, use the kebab-case form to ensure consistent slicing across inherited profiles.

---

# QA Artifacts

After a successful build, inspect these files in `output/`:

| Artifact | Content |
|---|---|
| `output/qa.json` | Errors, warnings, info counts |
| `output/qa-time-report.json` | Per-resource build timing |
| `output/qa-time-report.tsv` | TSV version of timing report |

A build is considered clean when `output/qa.json` reports `EXIT:0` with no new errors.
